explainBack.question: If Claude no longer makes me pick Chat or Cowork, why do I still have to make a decision before handing over a longer task?
explainBack.answer: Because the merge removed only the entry doorway, not the control over actions. Once a task begins, Claude either asks before each action (Manual) or reduces check-ins (Auto), and that setting applies to the whole conversation. The reader also still chooses which inputs Claude may use and whether work runs locally (Desktop must stay open) or in the cloud. So the surviving decision is authority over actions and inputs, not which interface to enter.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must cite the Manual/Auto distinction, conversation-wide scope of the setting, and the local-versus-cloud execution boundary, without claiming the merge guarantees task success.
explainBack.assessment: The artifact fully supports this explain-back: P005 supplies Manual/Auto and conversation scope, P007 supplies the execution boundary, P008 compresses the residual-decision point, and P004 preserves the no-guarantee limit.

unseenTransfer.scenario: After the merged experience reaches her account, a reader asks Claude to rename and reorganize 400 vacation photos in local folders overnight, planning to close her laptop and let it finish while she sleeps.
unseenTransfer.question: Will the job finish overnight, and what setting should she choose given the files are irreplaceable?
unseenTransfer.answer: It will not finish if the laptop closes: the article says local file work needs Claude Desktop open, so an overnight closed-laptop run only works for cloud tasks, and her photos live on the machine. Because renames touch irreplaceable files, she should keep the conversation on Manual so Claude asks before each destructive action, name exactly which folders it may touch, and spot-check the renaming pattern on a small batch before authorizing the rest.

unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly: both the execution-location constraint and the permission model produce a specific, correct decision in this new situation, confirming the explanation is generative rather than example-bound.
